messages:
Maria T.: Heads-up — new HF model bring-up (hf/gpt-small-embed) shows embedding quality regression vs our Redwood conversion. Cosine down from ~0.95 to ~0.86 on our eval set. Suspect tokenizer/pooling/truncation mismatch.
Jonathan L.: ouch. any quick repro?
Maria T.: repro steps:
```
# load HF -> our converter -> embed
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/gpt-small-embed')
# converter currently saves tokenizer config.json with truncation_side='left' (??)
# we call: tokenizer(texts, padding='max_length', truncation=True, max_length=512)
# pooling: we extract token index 0 as CLS (assume special token), but HF model uses BOS instead
```
Result: batch mean cosine to HF baseline = 0.86. If I force add_special_tokens=False at encode time and then mean-pool tokens, cosine goes back to 0.94.
Kevin S.: hmm that smells like special_tokens_map or chat template insertion. Did the conversion preserve `special_tokens_map.json` and `tokenizer_config.json` fields like `add_bos_token`?
Maria T.: I inspected the converted artifacts — `special_tokens_map.json` exists but our converter overwrites `tokenizer_config.json` and sets `model_max_length=1024` and `truncation_side='right'` unconditionally. HF original had `truncation_side='left'`.
Jonathan L.: truncation_side could change which suffix/prefix tokens are kept. For short texts maybe not, but for reranker (long concat of query+doc) it matters. Also CLS pooling: are we using the token index 0 or searching for `cls_token`?
Maria T.: currently index 0. HF model uses BOS (token id 1) as prefix; our conversion was inserting an extra system prompt token before it when creating the chat template, shifting the position. So index 0 is not reliable.
Kevin S.: Can you paste the snippet where we build the chat prompt? maybe the template adds `"); system: ..."` or something and we then tokenise the whole string.
Maria T.: snippet: ```
chat_prompt = f"<SYSTEM>{system_prompt}</SYSTEM>\n{user_text}"
tokens = tokenizer(chat_prompt, return_tensors='pt', padding=True)
# then we take tokens.input_ids[:,0] as CLS
```
Jonathan L.: yep — system wrapper changed token offsets. Two possible fixes: 1) use tokenizer.special_tokens_map to find `cls_token` or `bos_token` id and locate that in input_ids, 2) switch to deterministic pooling like mean pooling over non-padding tokens (and ensure add_special_tokens handling).
Kevin S.: also run quantization check — 8-bit/4-bit can change embedding L2 slightly. But 0.86 vs 0.95 is too big for quant alone. Run: fp16 vs int8 vs dynamic-4bit with the same tokenization/pooling.
Maria T.: agreed. Quick numbers I ran earlier (small sample): fp16->baseline=0.95, int8->0.93, converter-with-trunc-side-right->0.86. So conversion is biggest culprit.
deploy-bot: deployment notice: model hf/gpt-small-embed converted -> redwood-store/id: rwd-2026-11. queued for canary.
Jonathan L.: ACTIONS: Maria — update converter to retain `truncation_side` and preserve `add_special_tokens` semantics; Kevin — run quantization grid (fp16,int8,4bit) with both CLS-locating and mean pooling; I'll add a small eval that compares embedding cosines per sample and flags >0.03 drop.
Maria T.: sounds good. I'll also add an integration test that tokenizes with and without `chat_template` and asserts the CLS/bos index mapping is stable.
Kevin S.: I'll run the batch overnight and post results here. If we confirm converter bug, we should roll back canary. :+1:
Maria T.: thanks. tagging @kevin for follow-up.
Jonathan L.: thanks both. small note: also check `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)` call path — some HF tokenizers write `tokenizer_config.json` differently depending on tokenizer class (GPT2 vs Roberta). Converter should not normalize those fields away.
Maria T.: noted. I'll open a PR this afternoon. :rocket:
